Proposition 2.2. Let V = { 0 } be an ordered normed space whose cone has an interior point v . Then v is an order unit and the order unit norm ‖ · ‖ v is weaker than the original norm ‖ · ‖ on V . Moreover, every positive functional on V is continuous with respect to both norms.

Note that the two norms in Proposition 2.2 need not be equivalent, see, e.g., [6, Example 1.5.12]. For a detailed discussion in ordered Banach spaces, see [4, Proposition 2.11].

For an ordered vector space ( V, V + ) , a set S ′ of positive linear functionals from V to R is said to determine positivity if, for every v ∈ V , one has v ≥ 0 if ϕ ( v ) ≥ 0 for all ϕ ∈ S ′ . Note that, if V is an order unit space and Σ ⊆ V ′ + is given as in (2.1), then ext Σ determines positivity.

We will make use of the following two simple propositions.

Proposition 2.3. Let X be an ordered normed vector space and let S ′ ⊆ X ′ + . The following are equivalent:

- (i) The set S ′ determines positivity , i.e., for every x ∈ X , the inequality 〈 x ′ , x 〉 ≥ 0 for all x ′ ∈ S ′ implies that x ≥ 0 .
- (ii) The positive-linear hull of S ′ is weak-∗ dense in the dual wedge X ′ + .
- Proof. '(i) ⇒ (ii)' We show the contraposition. Let C ′ ⊆ X ′ + denote the weak-∗ closure of the positive-linear hull of S ′ and assume that there exists a point x ′ 0 ∈ X ′ + that is not in C ′ . By the Hahn-Banach separation theorem in the locally convex space X ′ with the weak-∗ topology, there exists a weak-∗ continuous functional x ′′ : X ′ → R and a number γ ∈ R such that 〈 x ′′ , x ′ 〉 ≥ γ > 〈 x ′′ , x ′ 0 〉 for all x ′ ∈ C ′ . Due to the weak-∗ continuity of x ′′ , there exists an element x ∈ X such that x ′′ is the point evaluation at x , see [13, § IV.1.2 on pp. 124-125]. It follows that 〈 x, x ′ 〉 ≥ γ > 〈 x, x ′ 0 〉 for all x ′ ∈ C ′ . Since 0 ∈ C ′ , we obtain γ ≤ 0 . Therefore, x is not in X + . As C ′ is a wedge, for every x ′ ∈ C ′ we have 〈 x, x ′ 〉 ≥ 0 , hence C ′ does not determine positivity.
- '(ii) ⇒ (i)' If x ∈ X satisfies 〈 x ′ , x 〉 ≥ 0 for all x ′ ∈ S ′ , then it follows from (ii) that the same inequality holds for all x ′ ∈ X ′ + . As X + is closed, this implies that x ∈ X + .

The following is a primal version of Proposition 2.3. As its proof is similar, we omit it.

Proposition 2.4. Let X be an ordered normed vector space and let S ⊆ X + . The following are equivalent:

- (i) The set S determines positivity of functionals in the sense that, for each x ′ ∈ X ′ , the inequality 〈 x ′ , x 〉 ≥ 0 for all x ∈ S implies that x ′ ≥ 0 .
- (ii) The positive-linear hull of S is weakly dense (equivalently, norm dense) in X + .

If the cone V + in an ordered vector space X has a base D , then x ∈ D is extremal if and only if x is an extreme point of D , see [6, Lemma 1.5.19]. The following result by Krein and Milman is given, e.g., in [13, §II.10.5 on p. 68].

Proposition 2.5. Let V be a locally convex Hausdorff space. Let Σ ⊆ V be compact and convex and let S ′ ⊆ Σ . If Σ = conv( S ′ ) then ext Σ ⊆ S ′ .
